Pipeline limit: batch reads with `paths` and asset ids FAIL ("no file is published at that path"), so each asset needs its own read call. Many calls can go in one message. Milestone 1 is about 85-90 calls; the whole game is about 250. Earlier readers already saved some files: the OPEN base 6d77cc9b... (Maps id); the OPEN and LAST STAND bases 47158da9... and 0e0ed6a0... (UI ids); Ves GIF e6071441...; BODY icon 933eb259...; skill icon 5987e17f...; icons 4e11ef2d..., 17a4faaf..., a8196f36... (24x24 glyph) and be0340e9... (16x16 pip); Lale GIF 5256eee6...; a 360x640 poster GIF b76debd0.... Stat, item and dice icons are 48x48 RGBA PNGs, pips are 16x16, glyphs are 24x24. Everything is raster, so no conversion is needed: files are served as static PNG/GIF. The real work is renaming to semantic paths, deduping by sha256 (the same file has a different id in each artifact) and rewriting /_blob/ references.

board_format_notes: Format. A .dc.html board is an HTML file that loads ./support.js (the DC runtime, which was not saved). The markup sits in an <x-dc> root. <helmet> holds head content: a Google Fonts <link> and a <style> block with the classes and @keyframes. After that comes one template tree with heavy inline style="" attributes. Templating is logic-less mustache: {{name}} or {{obj.field}} in attributes and text; loops are <sc-for list="{{arr}}" as="x" hint-placeholder-count="N">; conditionals are <sc-if value="{{bool}}" hint-placeholder-val="{{ false }}">. The hint-* attributes are editor placeholders only. Event props use React-style names bound to functions: onClick, onPointerDown/Move/Up/Leave, onWheel and onDoubleClick, plus ref="{{setCv}}" for a canvas. Handlers get React-like events (clientX, currentTarget, stopPropagation). <dc-import name="R6" view="pick"> embeds another board with props; R6Pick and R6Result are 500-byte wrappers that do this. Logic lives in <script type="text/x-dc" data-dc-script data-props='{...}'>. data-props declares editor props, e.g. R6 ring enum (9 styles, default segments), mood enum open/after/stand, view, and $preview size. The script is `class Component extends DCLogic` with React-class semantics: state = {...}, this.setState, this.props, componentDidMount/DidUpdate/WillUnmount. Its renderVals() returns a flat object of derived values and closures that the template reads. Assets are absolute /_blob/<32-hex> URLs that resolve only inside that artifact's asset store, so each must be downloaded, renamed and rewritten. Colours are hard-coded hex plus a few CSS custom properties: .th-meridian sets --ink, --dim, --line, --accent, --fill, --body and others. How much ports to React. R6.dc.html (1,119 lines, 87 KB): (a) the RollFX IIFE (lines ~186-805, ~55% of the file) is framework-free canvas code and copies almost verbatim into a TS module. It covers maths helpers, the d4-d20 die mesh and physics sim, the six SCENES (term, math, reel, cool, pulse, phys), plan(), and draw() with the gold explode burst, the nat-1 hard cut, the red crack lines, and the auto-fitting Archivo insult with white then red flash. The INSULT table at lines 351-359 includes 'YOU BRICKED IT, GENIUS.' under Tech. (b) ring() is a pure SVG-arc generator; keep only 'segments'. (c) The ~95 lines of CSS copy as-is into a global stylesheet, which cleans up the r3/r4/r5 prefixes. (d) The ~75-line template converts to JSX mechanically: sc-for to .map, sc-if to &&, style strings to objects or classes. (e) Component logic (~310 lines) needs rework, not copying. Pan, zoom and token drag become a shared hook. The pick, rolling (explosion gate auto-releases after 4 s, Skip) and done state machine moves to a store. startRoll currently uses client-side Math.random; the server must roll instead. RollFX.plan already takes a rolls array, so server results slot in. Hard-coded data must move to YAML/DB: Ves's name, role and stat dice, the skill/chrome list, the items, the people() list of 11, the mood image map, and the tab list (add GM). Token drag must emit WebSocket moves. Overall about 80% of R6 ports directly, and the rest is rewiring to server state. Event Horizon board, Maps/project/Main.dc.html (179 lines, 12 KB): close to 100% portable. It has proj(), defs() with the seat() helper and 16 tokens, the layer lists (bases, patches, glows, gases) with opacity toggles, and the same pan/zoom/drag code. The mood, Seal's box, hatch and gas toggles become server-side scene state driven from the GM tab. The Key board (80 lines) is a static POI list that becomes YAML.
